description: Cut, clear and cold, throwing light in every direction. Whatever swallowed it did not know what it had.
lore: Nothing here cuts a stone like this. What comes out of a creature comes out rough; this has fifty-eight faces and a girdle true the whole way round, and there is no wheel in Nangijala and no shop with the patience. So it was worn. Somebody carried it up out of [[lore/the_waking|the meadow]] in a ring or sewn into a hem, lost it in water, and something that swallows bright gravel got lucky.

The cutters can date the work — the style, the proportions, near enough the decade. That is the whole of what it will tell you. It gives up a workshop and a fashion and not one syllable about the hand it sat on, which is the ordinary cruelty of evidence: it outlasts the person and then answers a different question.
gm_notes: The owner is nobody in particular and must stay that way — the point is that a thing can survive its person and still be useless for finding them.
